text_blocks.snippet: Common scams targeting Central Illinois include AI-generated voice scams, law enforcement/prosecutor impersonation calls, fake traffic/DMV text messages, and romance or online marketplace scams.

text_blocks.snippet: Current Scam Trends in Central Illinois

list.snippet: AI Voice & Impersonation Scams: Scammers use artificial intelligence to clone human-like voices, pretending to be family members in distress or trusted contacts to trick victims into sending immediate money.

Federal Prosecutor & Law Enforcement Spoofing: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois and local sheriff's offices warn of callers spoofing official phone numbers. Scammers claim you have missed jury duty, an active arrest warrant, or fines, and demand payment via Bitcoin, gift cards, or wire transfers . (Note: Illinois does not use cash bail for warrants, and government agencies never call or text demanding payment).

Fake Traffic & DMV Text Messages: Phishing texts and emails impersonate the Illinois DMV or state transit authorities, claiming your license or vehicle registration will be suspended unless you pay an "outstanding traffic ticket" immediately through a link.
Romance and Social Media Marketplace Scams: Fraudsters build fake online relationships or list discounted/trending products on social media platforms, disappearing once payment is sent.

Establish a Safe Word: Families are encouraged by the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois to pick a secret code word to verify identity if a relative calls sounding distressed or asking for money .
Practice the Pause: Scammers create a false sense of urgency to keep you from thinking or calling a family member. Hang up and verify through an official number.
Never Pay via Unusual Methods: Real organizations will not ask you to pay via cryptocurrency (Bitcoin), peer-to-peer apps, or gift card numbers.
Do Not Click Links in Unsolicited Texts: Delete messages about unexpected package fees or traffic fines instead of clicking the links.

text_blocks.snippet: Who to Contact If You Are Targeted

list.snippet: Illinois Attorney General's Office (Consumer Fraud Hotlines):
File a report online via the Illinois Attorney General .
Local Law Enforcement: Call your local county sheriff's department or dial 911 if you lost money or feel physically threatened.
